topic: Wire antennas, arrays, Yagis and loading

questions.question: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed 180 degrees out of phase?

choices.C: A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array
choices.D: A figure-eight oriented along the axis of the array

questions.answer: A figure-eight oriented along the axis of the array

questions.question: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/4-wavelength apart and fed 90 degrees out of phase?

choices.B: A figure-eight end-fire along the axis of the array
choices.C: A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array
choices.D: Omni-directional

questions.question: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed in phase?

choices.C: A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array
choices.D: A figure-eight end-fire along the axis of the array

questions.answer: A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array

questions.question: What happens to the radiation pattern of an unterminated long wire antenna as the wire length is increased?

choices.A: Fewer lobes form with the major lobes increasing closer to broadside to the wire
choices.B: Additional lobes form with major lobes increasingly aligned with the axis of the antenna
choices.C: The elevation angle increases, and the front-to-rear ratio decreases
choices.D: The elevation angle increases, while the front-to-rear ratio is unaffected

questions.answer: Additional lobes form with major lobes increasingly aligned with the axis of the antenna

questions.question: What is the purpose of feeding an off-center-fed dipole (OCFD) between the center and one end instead of at the midpoint?

choices.A: To create a similar feed point impedance on multiple bands
choices.B: To suppress off-center lobes at higher frequencies
choices.C: To resonate the antenna across a wider range of frequencies
choices.D: To reduce common-mode current coupling on the feed line shield

questions.answer: To create a similar feed point impedance on multiple bands

questions.question: What is the effect of adding a terminating resistor to a rhombic or long-wire antenna?

choices.A: It reflects the standing waves on the antenna elements back to the transmitter
choices.B: It changes the radiation pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional
choices.C: It changes the radiation pattern from horizontal to vertical polarization
choices.D: It decreases the ground loss

questions.answer: It changes the radiation pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional

questions.question: What is the approximate feed point impedance at the center of a two-wire half-wave folded dipole antenna?

choices.C: 50 ohms
choices.D: 450 ohms

questions.question: What is a folded dipole antenna?

choices.B: A center-fed dipole with the ends folded down 90 degrees at the midpoint of each side
choices.C: A half-wave dipole with an additional parallel wire connecting its two ends
choices.D: A dipole configured to provide forward gain

questions.answer: A half-wave dipole with an additional parallel wire connecting its two ends

questions.question: Which of the following describes a G5RV antenna?

choices.A: A wire antenna center-fed through a specific length of open-wire line connected to a balun and coaxial feed line
choices.C: A phased array antenna consisting of multiple loops
choices.D: A wide band dipole using shorted coaxial cable for the radiating elements and fed with a 4:1 balun

questions.answer: A wire antenna center-fed through a specific length of open-wire line connected to a balun and coaxial feed line

questions.question: Which of the following describes a Zepp antenna?

choices.A: A horizontal array capable of quickly changing the direction of maximum radiation by changing phasing lines
choices.C: An omni-directional antenna commonly used for satellite communications
choices.D: A vertical array capable of quickly changing the direction of maximum radiation by changing phasing lines

questions.question: How is the far-field elevation pattern of a vertically polarized antenna affected by being mounted over seawater versus soil?

choices.B: Additional lobes appear at higher elevation angles
choices.C: Separate elevation lobes will combine into a single lobe
choices.D: Radiation at low angles increases

questions.question: Which of the following describes an extended double Zepp antenna?

choices.C: A center-fed 1.25-wavelength dipole antenna
choices.D: An end-fed 2-wavelength dipole antenna

questions.question: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally polarized antenna vary with increasing height above ground?

choices.A: The takeoff angle of the lowest elevation lobe increases
choices.B: The takeoff angle of the lowest elevation lobe decreases
choices.C: The horizontal beamwidth increases
choices.D: The horizontal beamwidth decreases

questions.answer: The takeoff angle of the lowest elevation lobe decreases

questions.question: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally-polarized antenna mounted above a long slope compare with the same antenna mounted above flat ground?

choices.A: The main lobe takeoff angle increases in the downhill direction
choices.B: The main lobe takeoff angle decreases in the downhill direction
choices.C: The horizontal beamwidth decreases in the downhill direction
choices.D: The horizontal beamwidth increases in the uphill direction

questions.answer: The main lobe takeoff angle decreases in the downhill direction

questions.question: How much does the gain of an ideal parabolic reflector antenna increase when the operating frequency is doubled?

choices.C: 4 dB
choices.D: 6 dB

questions.question: How can two linearly polarized Yagi antennas be used to produce circular polarization?

choices.A: Stack two Yagis to form an array with the respective elements in parallel planes fed 90 degrees out of phase
choices.B: Stack two Yagis to form an array with the respective elements in parallel planes fed in phase
choices.C: Arrange two Yagis on the same axis and perpendicular to each other with the driven elements at the same point on the boom and fed 90 degrees out of phase
choices.D: Arrange two Yagis collinear to each other with the driven elements fed 180 degrees out of phase

questions.answer: Arrange two Yagis on the same axis and perpendicular to each other with the driven elements at the same point on the boom and fed 90 degrees out of phase

questions.question: What is the most efficient location for a loading coil on an electrically short whip?

choices.A: Near the center of the vertical radiator
choices.B: As low as possible on the vertical radiator
choices.C: At a voltage maximum
choices.D: At a voltage null

questions.answer: Near the center of the vertical radiator

questions.question: Why should antenna loading coils have a high ratio of reactance to resistance?

choices.C: To maximize efficiency
choices.D: To minimize the Q

questions.question: Approximately how long is a Yagi’s driven element?

choices.C: 1/4 wavelength
choices.D: 1/2 wavelength

questions.question: What happens to SWR bandwidth when one or more loading coils are used to resonate an electrically short antenna?

choices.C: It is unchanged if the loading coil is located at the feed point
choices.D: It is unchanged if the loading coil is located at a voltage maximum point

questions.question: What is an advantage of top loading an electrically short HF vertical antenna?

choices.C: Higher losses
choices.D: Improved radiation efficiency

questions.question: What happens as the Q of an antenna increases?

choices.C: Gain is reduced
choices.D: More common-mode current is present on the feed line

questions.question: What is the function of a loading coil in an electrically short antenna?

choices.A: To increase the SWR bandwidth by increasing net reactance
choices.C: To lower the Q
choices.D: To resonate the antenna by cancelling the capacitive reactance

questions.answer: To resonate the antenna by cancelling the capacitive reactance

questions.question: How does radiation resistance of a base-fed whip antenna change below its resonant frequency?

choices.C: Radiation resistance becomes imaginary
choices.D: Radiation resistance does not depend on frequency

questions.question: Why do most two-element Yagis with normal spacing have a reflector instead of a director?

choices.C: Greater front-to-side
choices.D: Higher gain

questions.question: What is the purpose of making a Yagi’s parasitic elements either longer or shorter than resonance?

choices.C: Control of phase shift
choices.D: Minimize losses
